question: After a $20\%$ discount, a bag costs $\$60$.
What was the price before the discount?

beats.say: Most students get this wrong. After a twenty percent discount, a bag costs sixty dollars. What was the price before the discount?
Pause. What do you think the next step is?
Many add twenty percent of sixty, and get seventy two dollars.
But the twenty percent was taken from the original price, not from sixty. So sixty dollars is eighty percent of the original.
Find one percent: sixty divided by eighty, which is nought point seven five. Then times one hundred. The original price is seventy five dollars.
Check. Twenty percent of seventy five is fifteen. Seventy five minus fifteen is sixty.
Remember: sixty dollars is eighty percent of the original.

verify:
orig = Rational(75)
assert orig * Rational(80, 100) == 60
assert Rational(60, 80) == Rational(3, 4)
assert Rational(60, 80) * 100 == 75
assert orig * Rational(20, 100) == 15
wrong = 60 + Rational(20, 100) * 60
assert wrong == 72 and wrong * Rational(80, 100) != 60

youtube.title: Price after 20% off is $60. Original price? (Not $72)
youtube.description: A bag costs $60 after a 20% discount. Adding 20% of $60 gives $72 — wrong. $60 is 80% of the original, so the original is $75.
